answer: Gate every newcomer through one rate-limited onboarding wharf where it must lock a slashable bond and bind to a single hardware key. Each epoch a random beacon broadcasts a fresh nonce, and every identity has a narrow window to echo back a signature only its own silicon can produce. Clones crammed onto one machine cannot echo each beacon at once; their replies serialize into a late, correlated plume a jury flags, slashing the linked bonds. Faking N identities thus costs N separate live machines plus N bonds perpetually at risk: linear N times real hardware and capital, no pooling.
